subject.title: fix: tighten control ui input validation [AI]

question: Should merge patches globally reject the four legacy accessor-method key names even where the schema permits them as record IDs, or should filtering remain limited to keys that can mutate prototypes at that path?
rationale: The broader rejection is defense-in-depth rather than required by ordinary object writes, and accepting it intentionally changes existing configuration compatibility.

options.title: Preserve valid record IDs
options.body: Keep the four names allowed at schema-owned record-key paths while continuing to reject actual prototype-mutating keys and unsafe nested values.

options.title: Adopt global rejection
options.body: Explicitly make the names invalid across configuration, align schema and documentation, and provide an upgrade or doctor migration for affected stored config.

recommendation.title: Preserve valid record IDs
recommendation.body: Keep the four names allowed at schema-owned record-key paths while continuing to reject actual prototype-mutating keys and unsafe nested values.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice crosses the Gateway-facing config patch boundary and adjacent Control UI behavior that this person has maintained recently.
